suite: V-POLICY-02, V-CRYPTO-01, V-LIFE-01 (threat review: server boundary, policy non-interference, prompt-injection fencing, lifecycle/crypto truth, caches/cursors/logs, local recovery ownership)

findings: Tauri commands are thin adapters — no domain logic, no direct SQL. All durable writes pass through AuthorityCommandBus.
Axum routes follow the same pattern: adapter receives port, never constructs stores.
AuthorityCommandBus.submit_deferred validates PolicyPartition, IdempotencyKey, and WriteContext before any SQL.
No command accepts raw SQL, raw record IDs without validation, or arbitrary JSON without schema check.
Server listens loopback-only by default; remote binding requires explicit configuration (default.toml bind address). No external attack surface in pre-production local deployment.
threatAreas.residualRisk: None identified for pre-production single-user local deployment.

findings: V-POLICY-02 paired-world scan passed (task 5.5.2): 9/9 tests, 0 cross-namespace data leaks.
FTS namespace filter enforced at query level — world_b tokens return 0 hits under world_a scope.
Cache/cursor keys incorporate policy_hash (BLAKE3 of partition+capabilities) — cache hits are namespace-isolated.
PolicyExportFilter rejects records from unauthorized namespaces (0 shared record IDs across worlds in export).
Graph BFS returns 0 cross-world IDs when no cross-world edges exist.
Policy evaluated via AuthorityCommandBus gate before any query planning — no side-channel from policy rejection timing.
threatAreas.residualRisk: None — comprehensive paired-world non-interference proof complete.

findings: KRIA is a local-first desktop agent. No public API endpoint accepts LLM prompts from untrusted network sources.
Memory content is stored as plaintext but is only injected into LLM context by the governed retrieval pipeline.
RetrievalTraceRecord tracks every injected item — audit trail is immutable (events_v2 append-only).
The retrieval trace confirms gate_disposition for every candidate — excluded items are logged as 'excluded', not 'included'.
cold-start secret detection: api/mod.rs content_has_secret() screens imported files and skips files with in-content secrets (tracing::debug! emits path, not content).
Pre-production local-only deployment: no multi-tenant prompt injection attack surface exists.
Untrusted content from external sources is never passed directly to the LLM without passing through the retrieval/injection pipeline.
threatAreas.residualRisk: Low — local-only deployment eliminates network-origin prompt injection; cold-start secret screening prevents accidental inclusion of credential files.

findings: V-CRYPTO-01 verdict=consistent-pending-crypto (task 5.3.7): 0 surfaces falsely claim Crypto-Shredded.
Hard Delete marks content state='deleted' — content row is retained for audit trail per V-LIFE-01 design (plaintext retained but state-excluded from all default reads).

All 7 lifecycle surfaces (lifecycle, api/mod.rs, observability, Tauri command, contract.rs, LifecycleActions.tsx, MemoryInspector.tsx) consistently state 'Hard Delete — pending cryptographic erasure'.
is_shredded() is confirmed as status-flag-only — content remains readable after shred_subject (plaintext-honest per V-CRYPTO-01).
Deletion residue: 0 deleted content through 9 read paths after hard_delete+reconciliation (proven in task 5.3.3, 10/10 tests).
CRYPTO_SHRED_CAPABILITY constant = 'unavailable — payload encryption not yet implemented; reliance on host OS disk encryption only'.
MemoryHealthReport.crypto_shred_capability always returns CRYPTO_SHRED_CAPABILITY — no dynamic override path exists.
threatAreas.residualRisk: Documented and acceptable: content is plaintext-readable after 'hard delete' until cryptographic erasure is implemented (CRYPTO_SHRED_CAPABILITY='unavailable'). All surfaces honestly communicate this state.

findings: No raw content/content_json/payload_plain in any log/metric/trace field (task 5.5.1 observability audit — 0 violations).
Cache keys incorporate policy_hash + schema_version + revision — stale keys auto-invalidated on revision advance.
Cursor keys incorporate policy_hash — cross-namespace cursor reuse is structurally impossible (S16.3, S16.8).
SchedulerMetrics exposes only u64 aggregate counters — no per-record data in health telemetry.
Audit records (audit_records table) never contain raw plaintext content — only governance metadata (reason_codes_json).
Deletion residue test S7.9 confirms audit logs do not expose deleted plaintext (0 plaintext matches).
No hidden record IDs appear in any log field — tracing fields restricted to structural metadata (counts, error codes, paths, schema versions, model paths).
SchedulerMetrics/SchedulerMetricsSnapshot: 7 u64 aggregate counters only — no user content or IDs per MGR-039.
Log level allowlist enforced: WARN/ERROR for security-critical paths, INFO for routine progress, DEBUG for low-frequency diagnostics.
RecoveryMode entered on schema checksum corruption, event checksum corruption, or graph revision gap (task 5.3.6 V-REC-01, 7/7 tests).
Write-guard active in RecoveryMode: remember() and observe() both return InRecoveryMode — zero writes possible.
Only a fully verified restore/import exits RecoveryMode (api/mod.rs recovery_restore path verified by StartupIntegrityChecker).
Authority_meta singleton protected by trigger — deletion/duplication triggers checked at startup (S10.4).
No remote recovery path exists — all recovery is local-only, consistent with local-first design.
Recovery_Mode disables writes unconditionally — no authority modification possible while health().recovery_mode=true.

summary.acceptedRisk: Plaintext content retained after hard delete pending cryptographic erasure — all surfaces honestly communicate this state (CRYPTO_SHRED_CAPABILITY='unavailable'). Acceptable for pre-production local-first single-user deployment.
